com.prestol.building.brewer.desc: Dries grain and brews the beers and whiskeys of Let's Do Brewery. Finer drinks need a higher level.
com.prestol.building.winemaker.desc: Presses grapes and apples and ferments the wines and ciders of Let's Do Vinery. Finer wines need a higher level.
prestol.advice.all_good: All is well. Grow your settlements, trade and keep your borders.
prestol.advice.ally: Make an alliance with your neighbours: allies pay no duty and help in war.
prestol.advice.besieged: "%s" is besieged! Lead your troops to the town hall: while a defender lives there the siege stands still.
prestol.advice.edict: Issue an edict in "%s", say a Festival or a Harvest edict.
prestol.advice.found: Found your own realm: type a name on the right and press Found.
prestol.advice.grow: "%s" grows towards %s: citizens %s, town hall %s, buildings %s.
prestol.advice.hire: Hire a trader: he sells the surplus of "%s" and brings what is lacking by himself.
prestol.advice.invite: The free settlement "%s" is near: invite it into the realm.
prestol.advice.invited: You are invited into the realm "%s": accept below.
prestol.advice.land: Take the land round your settlements: %s plots more are yours to take.
prestol.advice.law: You can enact a law: %s free places.
prestol.advice.no_colony: Place a MineColonies town hall: your hamlet begins with it. The supply camp or ship gives you one.
prestol.advice.no_tower: "%s" has no guard tower. Build one: a garrison of its people will stand in it.
prestol.advice.tower_lack: The tower in "%s" lacks: %s. Put it in the tower or the warehouse.
prestol.advice.unpaid: The treasury cannot pay the soldiers: raise the tax or hire a trader.
prestol.advice.warehouse: Build a warehouse in "%s" and you can hire a trader.
prestol.army.conscript_home: %s came home to %s after his service.
prestol.army.conscripted: %s took up arms and joined the garrison of %s.
prestol.army.cost.shieldman: a shield, a sword and food
prestol.army.cost.spearman: a spear, pike or halberd and food
prestol.army.deserted_unpaid: %s garrison soldiers deserted: unpaid for too long, their spirit broke.
prestol.army.guards_freed: «%s»: the MineColonies guards are plain citizens now — a Hundred Years War garrison keeps watch.
prestol.army.need.spawn: the soldier did not appear (see the server log)
prestol.army.no_hyw_workers: No workers here: MineColonies citizens do that work.
prestol.army.no_recall: Garrison soldiers and militiamen cannot be put into a scroll.
prestol.army.order_too_far: Too far: orders reach 512 blocks and loaded land only.
prestol.army.routed: Your soldiers waver: %s flee the battle!
prestol.army.starving: %s is starving: no food in the tower, the warehouse or the baggage.
prestol.book.admin_note: Everything is here: realms, wars, sieges. Deleting a realm cannot be undone.
prestol.book.army_intro: One soldier per building level. A recruit takes his weapon and food from the building itself, a warehouse or the town hall. Those serving stay; new ones come of the chosen kind.
prestol.book.army_keep_note: Those serving stay; new recruits come of the chosen kind.
prestol.book.army_none: No guard tower or barracks tower yet. Build them and each will keep a garrison.
prestol.book.army_off: Garrisons are off: they need the Hundred Years War mod and army.garrisonInsteadOfGuards.
prestol.book.army_pick: Pick a building on the left.
prestol.book.army_school: Trained by the %1$s, level %2$s: rank %3$s of %4$s, +1 every %5$s min.
prestol.book.army_task: Task: %s — set in the window of the tower, settings.
prestol.book.bond_liege_text: Our suzerain: we pay it %s%% of our taxes and fight its wars; it protects us.
prestol.book.bond_vassal_text: Our vassal: pays us %s%% of its taxes and fights our wars.
prestol.book.camp_hint: A war tent (banner, 3 wool, 2 sticks) set up near an enemy settlement is a camp: it feeds soldiers from the chests beside it, keeps the siege up and cuts off trade.
prestol.book.capital_needs: Only a town with at least %s citizens can be the capital.
prestol.book.chronicle_note: The mouse wheel turns the entries.
prestol.book.court_law_note: For %s days an outlaw is an enemy in the realm's lands: guards and soldiers attack him. The price (from the treasury) goes to whoever brings him down, or to the owner of the soldier who does.
prestol.book.court_titles_note: Titles follow holdings: a hamlet makes a knight, a village a baron, a town a count, three settlements a duke.
prestol.book.draw_step1: Open Xaero's world map (the button on the right or its key).
prestol.book.draw_step2: Hold the right mouse button and drag over chunks to select a rectangle.
prestol.book.draw_step3: Let go and choose "Prestol: take the land".
prestol.book.draw_step4: Select land you no longer want the same way and choose "Prestol: give the land up".
prestol.book.economy_off: Treasuries are off on this server.
prestol.book.enslaved: The people are enslaved: no sleep, and someone dies every dawn.
prestol.book.event_wait: The ruler or the chancellor decides.
prestol.book.fealty_break_note: Breaking the oath means war with the suzerain and its vassals.
prestol.book.fealty_demand_tip: Make them our vassals: they pay %s%% of their taxes and fight our wars, we protect them.
prestol.book.fealty_swear_tip: Become their vassal: pay %s%% of taxes, fight their wars, live under their protection. A vassal declares no wars of its own.
prestol.book.fealty_they_demand: They demand our fealty (%s%% of taxes).
prestol.book.fealty_they_swear: They are ready to swear fealty to us (%s%% of taxes).
prestol.book.flag_bad_url: An http:// or https:// link is needed
prestol.book.flag_drop_hint: Right mouse button paints white. You can drop a picture onto this window.
prestol.book.flag_loaded: The picture is on the cloth; paint over it if you like.
prestol.book.free_lord_text: You serve no realm yet. A settlement owner may found a realm or accept an invitation.
prestol.book.goal_tip: With enough subjects and towns the realm rises in rank: it may hold %s laws and its ruler takes a new title.
prestol.book.images_note: Any Immersive Paintings picture can be a flag. Upload your own in a painting's window.
prestol.book.immune_until: Protected until day %s: it cannot be taken.
prestol.book.kind_buy_tip: In a foreign settlement: buy from its market if the price is no higher. The treasury pays.
prestol.book.kind_load_tip: In your own settlement: take goods from the store.
prestol.book.kind_sell_tip: In a foreign settlement: sell to its market if the price is no lower. The money goes to the treasury.
prestol.book.kind_unload_tip: In your own settlement: hand goods to the store.
prestol.book.land_give_here_tip: Give up your plots 5×5 round you.
prestol.book.land_rules: You may take nobody's land next to yours, within %s chunks of a town hall. The limit grows with settlements, town hall levels and buildings.
prestol.book.land_take_here_tip: Take the plots round you (5×5 chunks), as far as your allowance goes. You may take unowned land next to yours.
prestol.book.law_lock: A new law can be enacted in %s.
prestol.book.legend_flags: Settlements fly their realm's flag; capitals have a crown, besieged ones crossed swords.
prestol.book.market_auto_tip: The settlement sells foreign merchants what lies in its stores beyond its needs, and buys what its people ask for and nobody in the colony can give them, and food when the larder runs low. Prices follow the worth of the goods: cheaper in plenty, dearer in need. Your own market lines come first.
prestol.book.market_note: Goods come from the warehouses and the town hall; money from and into the treasury.
prestol.book.markets_intro: A market tells foreign traders what the settlement sells and buys, and at what price.
prestol.book.need_settlement: Place a MineColonies town hall first — you need a hamlet of your own.
prestol.book.new_trader_tip: A caravan, a merchant with pack mules, is fitted out in a capital with a warehouse; a ship in a capital with a fisherman's hut, its harbour. The treasury pays.
prestol.book.no_decrees: The ruler (or a settlement's owner) issues decrees for the realm's settlements.
prestol.book.no_other_realms: There are no other realms yet.
prestol.book.no_paintings: Immersive Paintings is needed — without it the flag is drawn from the banner.
prestol.book.no_realm_no_banner: Only a realm has a flag.
prestol.book.no_realm_no_trade: Only a realm has a treasury and trade.
prestol.book.no_realm_no_war: Only a realm can make war or alliances.
prestol.book.no_xaero: No Xaero map: take land with the buttons on the left. With Xaero's World Map you can take land with the mouse and see the realms' borders.
prestol.book.offer_keep_tip: How much to keep: only what is above is sold.
prestol.book.offer_upto: while the store has less than %s, now %s
prestol.book.offer_upto_tip: Buy while the store holds less than this.
prestol.book.order_from_hand: Add an order for the item in hand
prestol.book.pick_settlement: Pick a settlement on the left.
prestol.book.preview: This is how the flag will look.
prestol.book.revolt_terms: A revolution may start from day %s if happiness is below %s. Stand at the town hall and hold it.
prestol.book.siege_rules: To take a settlement, stand at the enemy town hall and hold it: while a defender lives nearby — a garrison soldier, a militiaman, a player — the clock stops. Fleeing soldiers do not count.
prestol.book.stop_no_orders: No orders: he only rests here.
prestol.book.title: Book of the realm
prestol.book.trader_add_stop: Pick a settlement with the arrows and press "+" to add a stop.
prestol.book.trader_guards_tip: An escort costs %s coins a guard per leg and keeps bandits off on foreign and wild land.
prestol.book.trader_home_tip: Where the trader sets out from and hands in his goods. Click to pick another settlement of the realm with a warehouse (a ship: with a fisherman's hut).
prestol.book.trader_mode_auto_tip: The trader decides himself where to take the surplus of his home and where to buy what the realm lacks. Click to give him a route by hand.
prestol.book.trader_mode_route_tip: The trader follows your route and your orders. Click to let him find his own deals.
prestol.book.trader_mules_tip: Each pack mule carries 15 slots and costs %s coins.
prestol.book.traders_intro: A trader finds his own deals: he takes the surplus of his home where it sells and brings back what the realm lacks. You can also give him a route by hand. On the road you can haggle with the merchant: right-click him.
prestol.book.treasury_deposit: Pay in all the gold you carry
prestol.book.treasury_gold_note: A coin is a gold nugget, an ingot 9, a block 81. The ruler takes money out.
prestol.book.treasury_gold_note_member: A coin is a gold nugget, an ingot 9, a block 81. Every subject may pay in.
prestol.book.treasury_tribute_in: Tribute from "%s": +%s a day, %s more days
prestol.book.treasury_tribute_out: Tribute to "%s": -%s a day, %s more days
prestol.book.treasury_unpaid: Soldiers unpaid for %s days: they grumble.
prestol.book.treaty_cede_tip: Pick with the arrows a settlement that changes hands by the treaty, theirs or ours.
prestol.book.treaty_fealty_tip: Fealty by treaty: one realm becomes the other's vassal and pays it %s%% of its taxes.
prestol.book.treaty_tribute_tip: Tribute: how many coins a day and for how many days one side pays the other. 0 means none.
prestol.book.unrest: Unrest: day %s of %s — the settlement may break away.
prestol.book.use_banner: Fly the banner instead of the picture
prestol.book.war_rules: Pick a realm on the left: alliance, war, peace.
prestol.book.weariness_tip: Every day of war, every fallen soldier and every settlement lost wears the people down; a settlement taken cheers them. Weariness lowers happiness in every settlement of the realm and wears off in peace.
prestol.book.wp_tip: Add a way point where you stand: the trader comes to this stop through your points. A ship needs them on the water.

prestol.decree.crafts.desc: Workshops turn out more and train faster.

prestol.event.bad_harvest.a_done: Bread was shared out; "%s" thanks its ruler.
prestol.event.bad_harvest.b.tip: Free, but for a whole day the people sulk and the fields yield less.

prestol.guide.army.1: MineColonies guard towers and barracks towers keep a garrison of Hundred Years War soldiers instead of guards: %s per building level. Warriors, spearmen, shieldmen, archers or crossbowmen are chosen on the Army page.
prestol.guide.army.2: A soldier is one of your citizens: an idle citizen takes up arms and moves to the tower, and when the garrison is dismissed he comes home with his name and skills. A fallen soldier is a dead citizen.
prestol.guide.army.3: A recruit needs a weapon (sword, spear, shield, bow or crossbow with arrows) and food, taken from the tower itself, the warehouse or the town hall. A new soldier comes every %s s until the garrison is full; no recruits come during a siege.
prestol.guide.army.4: The archery trains marksmen and the combat academy trains the foot: +1 rank every %s min. The garrison's task (guard, patrol, follow a player) is set in the tower window, Settings tab.
prestol.guide.army.5: There are no Hundred Years War workers here: MineColonies citizens do their work.
prestol.guide.banner.1: A realm has a colour and a coat of arms taken from its MineColonies colony flag. A realm standard, a Betsy Ross flag on a pole, costs %s wool and a stick and is handed out on the Banner page. The realm's flag flies over every town hall and Hundred Years War armies carry it.
prestol.guide.banner.2: You can draw your own flag: Banner → "Draw your own flag…". There are a brush, a fill, a picker, paints and any colour of your own, undo (Ctrl+Z) and mirror. The ruler draws and raises the flag.
prestol.guide.banner.3: A ready picture can be loaded from a link (png, jpg, gif) or simply dropped as a file onto the editor; touch it up before raising it.
prestol.guide.camps.1: A war tent (a flag or a banner, three wool, two sticks) is pitched during a war within %1$s blocks of an enemy settlement's town hall, usually outside its walls. That is where the realm's army makes camp.
prestol.guide.camps.2: Chests and barrels beside the tent are the camp's stores: the realm's soldiers nearby eat from them. By the camp soldiers fight as on their own land, while the besieged defenders lose heart. While the camp stands the siege holds for up to %1$s min even with the army away from the town hall, and traders of other realms keep out of the settlement.
prestol.guide.camps.3: The tent can be burnt or broken, a hard blow to the besiegers. When the war ends the camp is struck and the tent comes back.
prestol.guide.camps.4: Hundred Years War siege engines (rams, trebuchets, cannons) break walls only in settlements of a realm you are at war with and in the wild. Peaceful, allied and your own settlements are left alone.
prestol.guide.court.1: The ruler appoints a treasurer (treasury, taxes, duties, traders), a marshal (every garrison) and a chancellor (admissions and the law) on the Court and Law page. An owner or officer of one of the realm's settlements can be appointed.
prestol.guide.court.2: Lords carry titles by their holdings: a hamlet makes a knight, a village a baron, a town a count, three settlements a duke; the ruler is a prince, a king or an emperor. Titles show before names in chat and the player list.
prestol.guide.court.3: The ruler or the chancellor can outlaw a player for %1$s days with a price on his head from the treasury. The realm's guards and soldiers attack him in its lands, and whoever brings him down claims the price. A pardon returns it to the treasury.
prestol.guide.court.4: Whoever robs a realm's caravan in peace becomes an outlaw there himself.
prestol.guide.decrees.1: A decree is a temporary measure for one settlement: a festival, a great building, mobilisation, a harvest decree and more. After a decree you must wait before issuing it again. In the capital decrees are %s%% stronger.
prestol.guide.decrees.2: A law holds in the whole realm until it is repealed. The number of laws depends on the realm's rank; after a repeal a new law can only be enacted after %s min.
prestol.guide.drinks.1: With Let's Do Brewery and Vinery a colony gets a brewer's hut and a winemaker's hut. Place them with the build tool: packs "Prestol: Brewery" and "Prestol: Winery".
prestol.guide.drinks.2: The hut block is crafted like a MineColonies hut: planks around, the golden sceptre on top and a wooden brewing station (brewer) or a fermentation barrel (winemaker) in the middle.
prestol.guide.drinks.3: The brewer dries grain and brews beer and whiskey; the winemaker presses grapes and apples and makes wines and ciders. He orders hops, barley, grapes, bottles and water buckets through the warehouse. The finest drinks open at hut levels 2 and 3.
prestol.guide.events.1: About every %1$s game days, while the ruler or the chancellor is about, something befalls the realm: a bad harvest, a fair, a wandering knight, bandits on the roads, a fever, a rich vein, a year of plenty, a wedding at court.
prestol.guide.events.2: An event comes to the chat with two answers (click one) and shows on the first page of the book. Hover over an answer to see what it gives and what it costs.
prestol.guide.events.3: The answers change the treasury, the stores, the people's happiness and work, the warriors' strength and the safety of the roads for a day or two. If nobody answers within a game day, things take their course, as with the second, free answer.
prestol.guide.fealty.1: A realm may swear fealty to another, or the other may demand it; when both agree, the lesser becomes a vassal. Fealty can also be a term of a peace treaty. There is one rank of vassals only: a vassal has no vassals of its own.
prestol.guide.fealty.2: A vassal pays its suzerain %1$s%% of its taxes every day. They are allies: they trade without duties and stand by each other: the suzerain's wars call the vassal in, an attack on the vassal calls in the suzerain. The suzerain's peace is its vassals' peace with the same enemy.
prestol.guide.fealty.3: A vassal declares no wars of its own. The suzerain may release a vassal, and a vassal may declare independence, which means war with its suzerain.
prestol.guide.founded: "%s" is founded: this is your hamlet. Grow it into a village and a town, then found a realm. The Realm Book (%s) tells how in its Guide.
prestol.guide.lands.1: A realm takes land by chunks on the Xaero world map: hold the right mouse button, drag a rectangle and choose "Prestol: take land". Only unclaimed land next to your own, within %s chunks of a town hall, can be taken.
prestol.guide.lands.2: Land limit: %1$s chunks per settlement, %2$s per town hall level and %3$s per building. The realm's lands are painted in its colour on the map, and its banner flies over its settlements.
prestol.guide.militia.1: When a town hall is besieged, its people take up arms: a militia gathers at the town hall, one man per %s adult citizens, more in villages, towns and the capital. A militiaman is a citizen: the fallen do not come back.
prestol.guide.militia.2: The town hall window has a "Hire mercenaries" button: the squad takes %1$s gold ingots per man, follows the hirer and serves for %2$s min. Mercenaries bring their own bread.
prestol.guide.morale.1: Every soldier has a spirit from 0 to 100: look at one of yours to see it over the hotbar, and find it for each tower on the Army page. It drifts towards what his situation deserves: food, pay, own or enemy land, his lord nearby, experience and the odds in battle. It falls faster than it rises.
prestol.guide.morale.2: A soldier at 80 or more hits harder, below 40 softer. If his spirit drops below %1$s in battle he flees from the foes, keeps out of fights and holds no ground in a siege for half a minute, then rallies.
prestol.guide.morale.3: A comrade falling nearby shakes the spirit (veterans stand firmer), a foe falling lifts it. The death of their lord is a heavy blow. Keep your army fed, in numbers and under your banner: the realm's standard (the book gives it on the Banner page) carried by one of your men nearby lifts the soldiers' spirit.
prestol.guide.morale.4: A garrison left unpaid for days loses heart and scatters: the recruits go home as citizens.
prestol.guide.provisions.1: Every soldier carries provisions, 0 to 100%%. A full stock lasts %s game days. Soldiers do not need Hundred Years War supply: they eat ordinary food.
prestol.guide.provisions.2: Below 60%% a soldier refills on his own: from his tower, from the warehouse and town hall of his owner's or his realm's settlement, from Hundred Years War supply points, or from his commander's pack when he is near.
prestol.guide.provisions.3: A hungry soldier weakens, a starving one also slows down, and after %s game days of hunger he deserts: a drafted citizen goes home. Look at your soldier to see his rank and provisions over the hotbar.
prestol.guide.realm.1: A settlement owner founds a realm on the Realm page: give it a name and the settlement becomes its capital. A proper capital is a town with at least %s citizens: only such a town can be made the capital later, and the more citizens it has, the more settlements the realm can take.
prestol.guide.realm.2: A realm may hold %1$s settlements and one more for every %2$s citizens of its capital. The ruler invites free settlements on the Settlements page, and owners may ask to join. Settlements stay with their owners.
prestol.guide.realm.3: A realm rises in rank: Principality → Kingdom (%1$s subjects and %2$s towns) → Empire (%3$s subjects and %4$s towns).
prestol.guide.realm.4: The ruler decides on war and peace, moves the capital and enacts laws. During a war the realm cannot be disbanded and the capital cannot be moved.
prestol.guide.settlements.1: Every MineColonies colony is a settlement. A hamlet is any settlement. A village needs %1$s citizens, a level %2$s town hall and %3$s buildings; a town %4$s citizens, a level %5$s town hall and %6$s buildings. Only finished buildings count.
prestol.guide.settlements.2: If citizens or buildings are lost, a settlement declines and loses its tier. The higher the tier, the larger its militia and mercenary squads. The Settlements page shows what the next tier needs.
prestol.guide.settlements.3: Mind the happiness: below %1$s of 10 for %2$s days in a row, a settlement mutinies and leaves the realm.
prestol.guide.start.1: Prestol joins MineColonies colonies into realms. Everything is run from this book; it opens with %s. The pages are the ribbons on the right; hover a button or a line to see a hint.
prestol.guide.start.2: 1. Place a MineColonies town hall: this is your hamlet.
prestol.guide.start.3: 2. Build houses and workshops and bring in citizens: the hamlet grows into a village, then a town.
prestol.guide.start.4: 3. Found a realm on the Realm page: your settlement becomes its capital.
prestol.guide.start.5: 4. Invite other owners, take land, issue decrees, keep garrisons in your towers.
prestol.guide.start.6: 5. Once the realm is strong, make alliances, declare wars and take enemy settlements.
prestol.guide.trade.1: Every settlement of a realm has a market, and it trades by itself: it sells what lies in its stores beyond its needs and buys what its people ask for and nobody in the colony can give them (the requests MineColonies hands to the player), and food when the larder runs low. Prices follow the worth of the goods, worked out from recipes, so goods of other mods have a price too; cheaper in plenty, dearer in need. The owner may add lines of his own or switch the surplus trade off.
prestol.guide.trade.2: A realm hires traders: a caravan (a merchant with pack mules) costs %1$s coins, each mule %2$s more, a ship %3$s. A ship sails from fisher's hut to fisher's hut. A realm keeps at most %4$s traders.
prestol.guide.trade.3: You can also give a trader a route by hand, up to eight stops: load or unload at home, buy or sell at a foreign market with a price and an amount; the road can be laid out with waypoints.
prestol.guide.trade.4: A trader stays %1$s s in each settlement. Far from players he travels in the books; near you he travels for real, and you may meet him on the road or at sea.
prestol.guide.trade.5: A road through land that is neither yours nor an ally's is dangerous: unescorted traders may be robbed (%1$s%% a leg); a guard costs %2$s coins a leg. A slain merchant drops all his goods, and the robber is outlawed.
prestol.guide.trade.6: A hired trader finds his own deals: at home he looks at the markets within %1$s blocks, picks the trip worth the most (selling the surplus where it is wanted, bringing what is lacking, or carrying goods between your own settlements), loads up and sets out. Back home he hands in the goods and counts the takings. Press Go and that is all.
prestol.guide.trade.7: You may stop a merchant on the road and haggle: right-click opens the trading window. He sells his load %1$s%% above the market and buys what his realm lacks; payment is gold (nuggets, ingots and blocks). He does not trade with his realm's enemies or outlaws. Shift + right-click tells you who he is and where he is going.
prestol.guide.trade.8: Every %1$s game days (on average) a merchant from far lands comes to each settlement of a realm, by road or by ship to the fisherman's hut. He sells what the settlement lacks, buys up its surplus and stays by the town hall for a minute and a half: you can haggle with him. So trade goes on even in a world of a single realm.
prestol.guide.treasury.1: A realm's money is gold: a nugget is 1 coin, an ingot 9, a block 81. The ruler (or the treasurer) puts gold in and takes it out on the Treasury and Trade page.
prestol.guide.treasury.2: Once a game day settlements pay tax for each citizen: low %1$s, normal %2$s, high %3$s coins. Without tax citizens are happier, a high tax angers them. Besieged and enslaved settlements pay nothing.
prestol.guide.treasury.3: The treasury pays every garrison soldier %1$s coins a day. Short of money, soldiers get less and lose heart.
prestol.guide.treasury.4: Every income and expense is in the ledger. A realm may levy a duty on foreign traders; its own and its allies pay none.
prestol.guide.treaty.1: A ruler can offer peace on terms: a tribute (how many coins a day and for how many days one side pays the other) and the cession of a settlement, his own or the enemy's (a realm's last settlement cannot be ceded). The terms are set on the War and Peace page.
prestol.guide.treaty.2: The other ruler accepts peace on these terms or answers with his own. A ceded settlement changes hands as if taken: to the ruler of the receiving realm, protected from being taken again for a while.
prestol.guide.treaty.3: The tribute leaves the treasury once a game day. If the money falls short two days running the treaty is broken, the truce is gone, and war may be declared at once.
prestol.guide.war.1: The ruler declares war on the War and Peace page. The troops muster for %s min; no siege can start before that. Enemy players become Hostile in your settlements and the guards attack them.
prestol.guide.war.2: To take a settlement, stand by the enemy town hall (within %1$s blocks) and hold it for %2$s min. While a defender is alive nearby (a soldier, a militiaman or a player) the time stands still. If all attackers leave, the siege is lifted.
prestol.guide.war.3: A siege can only start while the settlement's owner or an officer is online.
prestol.guide.war.4: The capital falls last: it can only be besieged when the realm has no other settlements.
prestol.guide.war.5: The victor decides the settlement's fate: keep it, sack it (the loot chests by the town hall open only for the victors for %1$s min) or enslave its people (%2$s%% of the slaves die at each dawn). A taken settlement cannot be taken again for %3$s game days.
prestol.guide.war.6: Peace needs the consent of both sides and is followed by a truce of %s game days.
prestol.guide.war.7: The former owner of a taken settlement may raise a revolution after %1$s game days if its happiness is below %2$s: he must hold the town hall for %3$s min.
prestol.guide.war.8: A Hundred Years War captain gives orders within 512 blocks and loaded land. The war elephant walks over uneven ground and breaks through leaves.
prestol.guide.war.9: A long war wears the people down: every day of fighting, every fallen soldier and every settlement lost adds weariness, a settlement taken takes some away. At full weariness citizens are %1$s%% less happy. In peace weariness wears off within days.
prestol.guide.welcome: Welcome! Realms rule here: settlements grow, realms go to war and armies are raised from citizens. Press %s to open the Realm Book and read its Guide.
